items.headline: How Figma Uses AI Agents for Security
items.title: How Figma Uses AI Agents for Security
items.excerpt: Figma's engineering team documented how it built AI agents that triage security alerts, search past incidents, check internal systems and even draft code fixes. The agents learn from previous investigations, cutting repetitive review work.
items.rationale: Figma documents its own production agent stack — a concrete template for how a design org wires agents into repetitive review work.

items.headline: Photoshop Just Replaced Brightness and Contrast With Something Better
items.title: Photoshop Just Replaced Brightness and Contrast With Something Better
items.excerpt: Photoshop's Brightness/Contrast slider is now a Light adjustment layer with Camera Raw controls built in. Aaron Nace walks the optimal slider order and a double-mask glow technique.
items.rationale: A shipped Photoshop change that alters a daily editing habit tomorrow, with the exact slider order and masking technique spelled out.

items.headline: Can AI Now Design PCBs That Just Work?
items.title: Can AI Now Design PCBs That Just Work?
items.excerpt: OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra can take a schematic and output a complete KiCad board. Hackaday tests how far that claim survives contact with real hardware design constraints.
items.rationale: A hands-on reality check on schematic-to-board generation — the sharpest test yet of where AI CAD output stops being usable.

items.headline: OpenAI's controversial ChatGPT-6 Astra advert paints a sad vision of the future
items.title: OpenAI's controversial ChatGPT-6 Astra advert paints a sad vision of the future
items.excerpt: OpenAI's launch film for GPT-6 Astra has drawn a creative-industry backlash for the future of creative work it depicts. Creative Bloq unpacks why the ad landed so badly with designers.
items.rationale: The GPT-6 Astra launch film became a referendum on how AI vendors picture creative work — the framing designers now have to answer for.

items.headline: Five anti-AI designs that give an element of control back to humans
items.title: Five anti-AI designs that give an element of control back to humans
items.excerpt: Dezeen rounds up five products and graphics built as deliberate pushback against the AI boom, from a decoy font to hardware that refuses to connect - a design language for AI fatigue.
items.rationale: A working catalogue of anti-AI design moves — decoy fonts, disconnect-by-default hardware — that designers can borrow as a stance, not just a mood.
